authors: Project Numina (paper authors: Junqi Liu, Zihao Zhou, Zekai Zhu, Marco Dos Santos, Weikun He, Jiawei Liu, Ran Wang, Yunzhou Xie, Junqiao Zhao, Qiufeng Wang, Lihong Zhi, Jia Li, Wenda Li)
title: Numina-Lean-Agent, explained
h1: A Claude Code agent for Lean proofs, and the 17 problem statements it ships with
lead: Numina-Lean-Agent is mostly Python, prompts and tool wrappers that drive Claude Code to write Lean 4 proofs. The Lean it ships is a small problem set: the twelve Putnam 2025 problems and five miniF2F problems, written as formal statements whose proofs are deliberately left as sorry. Only one of the seventeen, a miniF2F divisor-sum fact, has a proof here, a single decide. The agent's finished Putnam proofs live in a separate repository.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of project-numina/numina-lean-agent: what the agent does, what its bundled Lean problem statements (Putnam 2025 and miniF2F) actually say, and how the harness checks a submitted proof.
startNote: Read About first: it says what the project is and which parts are not Lean at all. Then pick a problem: A2, the sine sandwich, is the easiest to read; A3, the ternary-string game, shows how a competition game gets encoded; amc12a_2021_p7 is the only statement that comes with a proof.
sizeNote: About 190 lines of Lean in 17 problem files (12 Putnam 2025, 5 miniF2F), plus a one-line placeholder library. The rest of the repository is Python, Markdown prompts and shell scripts.
agentCtx: project-numina/numina-lean-agent: a Claude Code based agent (Python harness, prompts, CLI skills) for Lean 4 theorem proving, shipping Putnam 2025 and miniF2F problem statements left as sorry.

gloss.Fin: Lean's Fin n: the numbers 0, …, n−1. In A3 a digit is a Fin 3. In A5 a permutation acts on Fin (n+1). Mathlib gives Fin n arithmetic modulo n.
gloss.Finset.univ: Mathlib's Finset.univ: the finite set of all elements of a finite type, such as all strings of length n.
gloss.Finset.card: Mathlib's Finset.card: the number of elements of a finite set.
gloss.Finset.sum: Mathlib's big-operator sum Σ over a finite set.
gloss.Finset.range: Mathlib's Finset.range n: the finite set {0, 1, …, n−1}.
gloss.Nat.divisors: Mathlib's Nat.divisors n: the finite set of positive divisors of n. It is computed by testing every number from 1 to n.
gloss.Nat.gcd: The greatest common divisor of two natural numbers.
gloss.IsGreatest: Mathlib's IsGreatest S a: a is in S and every element of S is at most a.
gloss.IsLeast: Mathlib's IsLeast S a: a is in S and every element of S is at least a.
gloss.Equiv.Perm: Mathlib's Equiv.Perm α: the permutations (bijections) of α.
gloss.Prop: Lean's type of propositions. MatrixProp and IsRollout are Props, not runnable checks.
gloss.Bool: Lean's two-valued type. In B1 it serves as the two colours.
